sources.title: Fundamental Information Analysis
sources.mechanism_summary: Fundamental operating and accounting signals can contain information associated with earnings persistence and value relevance beyond headline earnings.
sources.claim_boundary: The paper supports information-content relations for selected fundamental signals; it does not establish that a generic driver tree is universally causal or universally predictive across sectors and regimes.

sources.title: Fundamental Analysis, Future Earnings, and Stock Prices
sources.mechanism_summary: Fundamental signals are empirically related to subsequent earnings changes and analyst forecast revisions, with context conditioning affecting information content.
sources.claim_boundary: Observed predictive associations do not by themselves identify causal effects, and signal usefulness is context dependent rather than a universal fixed checklist.

sources.title: Ratio Analysis and Equity Valuation: From Research to Practice
sources.mechanism_summary: Financial statement analysis can be organized hierarchically, separating operating from financing activities and treating lower-level ratios as finer information for higher-level future payoff ratios.
sources.claim_boundary: A hierarchical ratio architecture is an analytical decomposition and forecasting scaffold, not proof that every lower-level ratio is a causal primitive or that the same hierarchy transfers unchanged across industries.

sources.title: Accounting Earnings and Cash Flows as Measures of Firm Performance: The Role of Accounting Accruals
sources.mechanism_summary: Accruals can improve earnings as a measure of performance when raw cash flows suffer more from timing and matching problems, particularly over shorter measurement intervals and longer operating cycles.
sources.claim_boundary: Cash flow is not automatically economically superior to accrual earnings; observed earnings-cash divergence must be interpreted through timing, matching, working-capital and investment context.

sources.title: Do Stock Prices Fully Reflect Information in Accruals and Cash Flows About Future Earnings?
sources.mechanism_summary: The persistence of current earnings into future earnings differs with the relative magnitudes of accrual and cash-flow components, and market prices in the studied sample did not fully reflect that information.
sources.claim_boundary: The result is a sample-specific empirical relation and market-pricing finding; it is not a fraud diagnostic and does not imply that all accruals are low quality.

sources.title: The Quality of Accruals and Earnings: The Role of Accrual Estimation Errors
sources.mechanism_summary: Working-capital accrual quality decreases as estimation errors increase; accruals shift cash-flow recognition across periods and therefore embed estimation uncertainty.
sources.claim_boundary: The accrual-quality construct covers one dimension of earnings quality and must not be converted into a generic misconduct or fraud score.

sources.title: Accrual Reliability, Earnings Persistence and Stock Prices
sources.mechanism_summary: Less reliable accrual categories are associated with lower earnings persistence, providing a balance-sheet reliability decomposition rather than a single undifferentiated accrual signal.
sources.claim_boundary: Reliability classification and persistence evidence do not prove manipulation, and estimated market mispricing is not a universal live-trading rule.

sources.title: Accrued Earnings and Growth: Implications for Future Profitability and Market Mispricing
sources.mechanism_summary: Accrual effects can be interpreted as part of a broader growth-in-net-operating-assets effect associated with future profitability and diminishing returns on investment.
sources.claim_boundary: An accrual signal may reflect normal investment and growth economics rather than accounting deterioration; Three-Statement Integrity must preserve this competing explanation.

sources.title: IAS 7 Statement of Cash Flows
sources.mechanism_summary: IAS 7 requires presentation of cash flows classified as operating, investing and financing activities and reconciliation of cash and cash equivalents with the statement of financial position.
sources.claim_boundary: IAS 7 defines reporting presentation and disclosure authority; it is not a predictive asset-pricing theory and is excluded from Shadow TheoryObject creation.
